source: Original (freshly authored 2026-09-29, HL syllabus 1.12/1.14, no calculator). Square roots of 5 - 12i by equating parts of (a + bi)^2: a^2 - b^2 = 5, 2ab = -12, giving +-(3 - 2i). Hence z^2 - 2z - 4 + 12i = 0, i.e. (z - 1)^2 = 5 - 12i, with roots 4 - 2i and -2 + 2i. Review of the conjugate root theorem (12-2CW): the roots are not a conjugate pair because a coefficient is non-real.

parts.label: a
parts.description: By writing (a + bi)^2 = 5 - 12i with a, b real, find the two square roots of 5 - 12i.
parts.tolerance: Accept +-(3 - 2i). Accept the modulus shortcut a^2 + b^2 = 13 combined with a^2 - b^2 = 5.
parts.notes: M1 for expanding and equating both real and imaginary parts (a^2 - b^2 = 5 and 2ab = -12). A1 for a = +-3 with b = -+2. A1 for both roots with the signs paired correctly. Pairing the signs wrongly (3 + 2i) earns the M1 only, since 2ab = -12 forces opposite signs.

parts.label: b
parts.tolerance: Accept the answers in either order and z = 1 +- (3 - 2i) expanded.
parts.notes: M1 for reducing the equation to the square root of 5 - 12i, by the quadratic formula (discriminant 4(5 - 12i)) or by completing the square, (z - 1)^2 = 5 - 12i. A1 for both solutions. A candidate who restarts with z = x + yi and solves correctly earns full marks, with the feedback note that (a) had already done the work.
parts.follow_through: Award the A1 for 1 +- the candidate's own square root from (a).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Explain why the two solutions in (b) are not a conjugate pair.

expected.answer: The coefficient -4 + 12i is not real; roots come in conjugate pairs only when all coefficients are real.

parts.tolerance: Accept any wording that identifies a non-real coefficient as the reason the conjugate root theorem does not apply.
parts.notes: R1 for naming the non-real coefficient (or 'the coefficients are not all real') as the reason. Saying only that 4 - 2i and -2 + 2i are not conjugates restates the question and earns nothing.

source: Original (freshly authored 2026-09-29, HL syllabus 1.13/1.14, no calculator). w = -8 + 8sqrt3 i = 16e^(2pi i/3). Fourth roots: 2e^(i(pi/6 + k pi/2)), i.e. 2e^(i pi/6), 2e^(2pi i/3), 2e^(-i pi/3), 2e^(-5pi i/6). First-quadrant root sqrt3 + i. Conjugate equation z^4 = -8 - 8sqrt3 i has the conjugate roots 2e^(-i pi/6), 2e^(-2pi i/3), 2e^(i pi/3), 2e^(5pi i/6).

parts.label: a
parts.description: Write w = -8 + 8sqrt3 i in the form re^(i theta), r > 0, -pi < theta <= pi.
parts.notes: A1 for modulus 16. A1 for argument 2pi/3. The marks are independent. An argument of -pi/3 (arctan(-sqrt3) with no quadrant check) loses the second A1.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Solve z^4 = w, giving each solution as re^(i theta) with -pi < theta <= pi.
parts.tolerance: Accept cis form. Accept the roots in any order.
parts.notes: M1 for modulus 2 with argument (2pi/3 + 2k pi)/4, or for one correct root followed by rotations of pi/2. A1 for any two correct roots. A1 for all four with every argument in the stated range; 2e^(7pi i/6) and 2e^(5pi i/3) are outside it and lose the final A1 unless converted.
parts.follow_through: Award the marks from the candidate's own modulus and argument in (a).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Write the first-quadrant solution in the form a + bi.
parts.tolerance: Accept 2(sqrt3/2 + i/2) simplified to sqrt3 + i.
parts.notes: A1 for sqrt3 + i. Decimal values (1.73 + i) earn nothing: exact values are required.
parts.follow_through: Award A1 for the candidate's own first-quadrant root from (b) correctly converted to Cartesian form.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Hence write down the four solutions of z^4 = -8 - 8sqrt3 i in the form re^(i theta).
parts.tolerance: Accept cis form, any order, and any equivalent arguments. Accept solving z^4 = 16e^(-2pi i/3) directly.
parts.notes: A1 for all four roots. The intended route is that -8 - 8sqrt3 i is the conjugate of w, so the solutions are the conjugates of those in (b). Three of four earns nothing.
parts.follow_through: Award A1 for the conjugates of the candidate's own roots from (b).

source: Original (freshly authored 2026-09-29, HL syllabus 1.14 with polynomial review, no calculator). Cube roots of unity 1, -1/2 +- (sqrt3/2)i. Hence (z - 1)^3 = 8 gives z - 1 = 2 omega, so z = 3, sqrt3 i, -sqrt3 i. Expanding gives z^3 - 3z^2 + 3z - 9 = 0, which factorizes over the reals as (z - 3)(z^2 + 3).

parts.label: a
parts.description: Find the three cube roots of 1 in the form a + bi.
parts.tolerance: Accept the factor route (z - 1)(z^2 + z + 1) = 0 with the quadratic formula. Accept (-1 +- sqrt3 i)/2.
parts.notes: M1 for a valid method: e^(2k pi i/3) with k = 0, 1, 2 (or -1), or the factorization of z^3 - 1. A1 for all three in Cartesian form. Answers left as e^(+-2pi i/3) earn the M1 only.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Hence solve (z - 1)^3 = 8, giving each solution in the form a + bi.
parts.tolerance: Accept 0 + sqrt3 i forms. Accept any valid route, including expanding and factorizing first.
parts.notes: M1 for z - 1 = 2 omega with omega each cube root of unity (or an equivalent method giving all three values of z - 1). A1 for all three solutions. Finding only z = 3 earns nothing.
parts.follow_through: Award the marks for 1 + 2 omega computed correctly from the candidate's own roots in (a).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Show that (z - 1)^3 = 8 can be written as z^3 - 3z^2 + 3z - 9 = 0 (answer given), and hence write z^3 - 3z^2 + 3z - 9 as a linear factor times a real quadratic factor.
parts.tolerance: The first step is show that (answer given). Accept the factors in either order.
parts.notes: First M1 for expanding (z - 1)^3 = z^3 - 3z^2 + 3z - 1 with the correct coefficients and signs, leading to the given cubic. Second M1 for any valid route to the factors: pairing the conjugate roots from (b) as (z - sqrt3 i)(z + sqrt3 i) = z^2 + 3, grouping z^2(z - 3) + 3(z - 3), or dividing by (z - 3). A1 for (z - 3)(z^2 + 3). A factorization with non-real coefficients, (z - 3)(z - sqrt3 i)(z + sqrt3 i), earns the second M1 only, since the question asks for a real quadratic factor.

source: Original (freshly authored 2026-09-29, HL syllabus 1.13/1.14, no calculator; review of de Moivre from 12-3CW). One cube root of w is 1 + sqrt3 i = 2e^(i pi/3), so w = 8e^(i pi) = -8. The other cube roots are -2 and 1 - sqrt3 i. The three roots form an equilateral triangle of side 2sqrt3 with area 3sqrt3.

parts.label: a
parts.description: One cube root of w is 1 + sqrt3 i. Use de Moivre's theorem to find w.
parts.tolerance: Accept 8e^(i pi) alongside -8. A correct binomial expansion of (1 + sqrt3 i)^3 reaching -8 also earns full marks.
parts.notes: M1 for writing 1 + sqrt3 i in exponential or polar form (modulus 2, argument pi/3) and cubing. A1 for w = -8. On the binomial route, add the feedback note that the question asked for de Moivre.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the other two cube roots of w in the form a + bi.
parts.tolerance: Accept the roots in either order. Accept any valid method.
parts.notes: M1 for any valid method: rotating 2e^(i pi/3) by +-2pi/3, solving z^3 = 8e^(i(pi + 2k pi)), or the conjugate root theorem (z^3 + 8 = 0 has real coefficients) with the third root from the sum of roots or by inspection. A1 for both roots in Cartesian form. Roots left as 2e^(i pi) and 2e^(-i pi/3) earn the M1 only.
parts.follow_through: Award the marks for the cube roots of the candidate's own w from (a).

parts.label: c
parts.description: The three cube roots are plotted on an Argand diagram. Find the exact area of the triangle they form.
parts.tolerance: Accept any exact equivalent, e.g. sqrt27.
parts.notes: M1 for any valid area method: base 2sqrt3 (from 1 + sqrt3 i to 1 - sqrt3 i) with height 3; the equilateral formula (sqrt3/4)s^2 with s = 2sqrt3; or three triangles from the origin, 3 x (1/2)(2)(2) sin(2pi/3). A1 for 3sqrt3. A decimal answer (5.20) loses the A1, since the exact area is asked for.
parts.follow_through: Award the marks for the area correctly computed from the candidate's own roots in (b).
